extracted.intended_audience: museum administrators and grant writers preparing IMLS Museums for America (MFA) applications
extracted.subtask_short: IMLS Museums for America grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used to prepare, review, and assess Museums for America (MFA) grant applications and funded projects (IMLS MFA program, FY2004–2010). Covers applicant eligibility, application contents, allowable activities, outcome/evaluation expectations, budget/matching rules, and reviewer considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility (institutional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicant museums are units of state or local government or tax-exempt, non-profit organizations located in the United States or territories. They must employ professional staff, have permanent institutional structures, serve essentially educational or aesthetic purposes, own or use tangible animate or inanimate objects, care for those objects, and exhibit them regularly to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a threshold/legal eligibility requirement — applications from organizations that do not meet these institutional characteristics are ineligible. See IMLS applicant guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant category alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply in one of three categories: engaging communities, building institutional capacity, or collections stewardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proposals should clearly identify and align activities, outcomes, and intended impacts with the selected category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to institution's strategic plan
rubrics_metrics.description: MFA supports projects that are clearly linked to the institution’s strategic plan and enhance its value to its community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application places significant focus on situating the proposed project within the institution’s strategic plan; reviewers expect explicit explanation of how the project advances stated strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must provide a needs assessment that justifies the project and situates it within institutional/community needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete evidence (audience data, institutional gaps, community needs) to demonstrate why the project is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience description
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must describe the intended audience for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include demographic/participation characteristics and explain how the project will reach and engage these audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, measurable outcomes for audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended audience outcomes must be described in terms of measurable changes in knowledge, skills, attitudes, or behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes should be specific and measurable (not just activities). Use outcome statements tied to metrics that can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The application includes an abstract that describes the lead applicant and any partners, the project time frame, intended audience, specific project activities, outcomes and products, and a description of intended audience outcomes in terms of measurable changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should concisely summarize the who/what/when/for whom/results and measurable outcomes to orient reviewers quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project narrative: design, resources, intended outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative must address project design, resources, and intended outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale, methodology/approach, staff and organizational capacity, timeline, and how resources will be used to realize outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes: products, measurable results, evaluation & reporting methods, sustainability, long-term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes must be described in terms of formal products, measurable results, evaluation and reporting methods, plans for sustaining the project over time, and long-term impact of the project after funding ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete deliverables, how success will be measured and reported, plans for continuation/funding after the grant, and expected enduring changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching funds / cost-sharing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by law, there is a one-to-one cost-sharing requirement; applicants must describe matching funds (money, staff time, in-kind services, etc.) equivalent to their grant award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and narrative should document match sources and demonstrate feasibility of the one-to-one match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable activities include a broad range of museum work, such as digitization and collections management, exhibit and program development and implementation, research and evaluation, and staff development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed activities should fit within these allowable categories; clarify primary activity area if multiple activities occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget includes evaluation and reporting costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant budgets are expected to include the costs of evaluation and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and budget for evaluation staff/time, instruments, data collection, and reporting deliverables (e.g., final performance report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of outcomes-based planning tools (logic models)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS provides an online course in outcomes-based planning and evaluation and encourages use of logic models and other planning tools in applicant evaluation plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ logic models to link inputs→activities→outputs→outcomes and to support measurable evaluation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limits and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants may be up to three years in length; for analysis projects are categorized as fewer than two years, two years, and more than two years, which may affect the range of activities and depth of impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose realistic timelines aligned with scope; reviewers consider whether proposed duration is sufficient to achieve stated outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award size ranges and analytic categories
rubrics_metrics.description: MFA grants range from $5,000 to $150,000; for analytic purposes award sizes are grouped into small (under $50,000), medium ($50,000–$99,000), and large (over $100,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose a budget scale appropriate to project scope; justify how award amount will accomplish outcomes and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary activity area selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are asked to choose the primary activity area of funding and resource investment from six areas: programming, exhibitions, collections, digitization, technology & online resources, or organizational activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the single primary focus for reporting/analysis even if project spans multiple areas; explain how other activities support the primary focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of award (self-assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/grantees may be asked whether the award amount was sufficient to complete the funded project (response categories: no, somewhat, yes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A realistic budget justification and explanation of how additional funds (if needed) would be secured strengthens assessment of sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review by field professionals using MFA guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS administers a rigorous peer review process that includes individual field reviewers and/or panel reviews; reviewers are professionals with knowledge of the kinds of activities described and they employ criteria identified in the MFA guidelines. The IMLS director makes final funding decisions based on reviewers’ evaluations and program/agency goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare applications to address common peer-review concerns: significance, feasibility, outcomes/measurement, institutional capacity, and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS encourages development of evaluation plans that document activities and audiences reached, project achievements, lessons learned, and immediate and longer-term outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation plans should specify methods, measures, timelines, responsible staff, data sources, and reporting mechanisms tied to stated outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships as an implementation dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are evaluated for the role and nature of partnerships (who the partners are, their contributions, and how partnerships support project goals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe partner roles, formal agreements (if any), resource contributions, and how partnerships extend reach or capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of final performance reports and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees submit final performance reports and supporting materials to IMLS; these reports are used in qualitative review and evaluation of project effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear documentation of activities, participant data, deliverables, lessons learned, and evidence of outcomes to include in final reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-effect evaluation dimensions (IMLS essential questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMLS sought to evaluate program effects using questions: impact on capacity building (training, policy implementation, institutional management); degree of success in growing/building capacity to serve communities; impact on communities served (education and exhibition outcomes); degree of success in developing/sustaining/expanding collections stewardship; success in achieving strategic goals as a result of funding; and sustainability after grant period ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These high-level effect dimensions are the outcomes IMLS expects MFA-funded projects to address and are useful frames for applicants to propose measures and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation challenges (to be reported/anticipated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report highlights implementation challenges as an analytic dimension (logistical, staffing, timeline, technical barriers) that affect project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and describe potential implementation risks and mitigation strategies in the application and evaluation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of primary project for post-grant effects analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For post-grant effects, the evaluation prioritized grantees’ earliest funded project (2004–2009) to assess effects at completion and several years later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing post-grant impacts, provide historical documentation and follow-up data demonstrating sustained outcomes beyond the grant period.
